Prevention: Crop rotation with cereal crops (Paddy-groundnut/ Maize-Groundnut is followed in a cropping year).
Effective weed control and field sanitation.
Avoiding accumulation and dumping of organic debris.
Deep burial of previous crops plant debris before sowing.
Sowing in raised beds or in broad bed furrows
Monitoring: Regular scouting during the rainy season.
Observe for fan shaped mycelium growth at the lower stem.
Leaves turn yellow followed by wilting of branches.
Disease is evident at 45-60 days after seedling emergence, strict monitoring for infestation during this period.
Yellowing of leaf and wilting of branches is considered as trigger to adopt the direct control measures.
Direct Control: Trichoderma viridie at a rate of 4 g per kg of seeds.
